This is Gay Valimont, candidate for FL-1.
In recent discussions, Governor DeSantis and Congressman Byron Donalds have clashed over issues of responsibility and service to Floridians, highlighting the critical importance of leadership that prioritizes the needs of the people. They have both come out of nowhere, during a Trump presidency, as an endorsed candidate for office. Coincidence?
We cannot let history repeat itself, and the way out is 25 days away: April 1st special elections. Help me help America.
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/71574A2F56537457766751757174494370706D6B796D467638784759302B72307368583777687A536E4C6E544E685A6F31534E775A4E46456866474270544941/editor_images/Screenshot%202025-03-06%20at%202.42.02%E2%80%AFPM.png]
I believe Florida deserves leaders who are focused on their duties and remain fully committed to serving our communities, not distracted by personal ambitions. It's time for our state to move away from political posturing and instead embrace transparency, accountability, and real solutions.
As your representative, I will ensure that Florida's leaders are held to the highest standards of integrity, with no room for neglect or failure to act when it matters most. These MAGA candidates are ready, pockets-lined, to simply receive a government pension and make headlines, NOT serve you.
Whether it’s securing healthcare access, addressing climate change, or ensuring that every voice is heard, my commitment is to serve and fight for all of us— not to use office as a stepping stone to higher power. We need leaders who will remain focused on their jobs and the welfare of every Floridian. That’s the kind of leadership I will bring to the table.
We’ve read this book before, and regardless of that outcome, we have an opportunity for Florida to flip a historically Red district; a huge step in the right direction. _**A message from our sponsor...**_

| | Dear Friend,

Learning about how early Christians worshipped and prayed, faced persecution and hardship, and settled theological disputes enriches our understanding of the faith. These lessons are especially important today, as Christians face increasing opposition from the culture.

But, beyond reading the New Testament and some of the stories of early Christian martyrs, it can be daunting to figure out how to proceed. The complicated history of imperial Rome, along with the foreign names and locations featured in early Christian history, can make understanding the most important historical points difficult.

To uncover this fascinating history, we've produced our online course, "[Ancient Christianity](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=66139f92e44e4b94a908a6305fc9d659&_e=fUE7pILIHcujUnmdFwZNfuRa9dsbijl2ILYrZ18PHojmul-oEJS_qon2WCPHWhLtD0YA2Rt-wK-iNvSx5lJaeR1i9V1Di345UaBMFWTT2QmwExj_gLYigdk6sxvT7pYgnfJghyc8NLfBw-HZBnrSCPkIaAmNYyrr9LNz-4cAm-A-4GtNtmb1gLSSK0jM56adiDhnwNj_gSUMWAGZhNcY165fptls0tjFt1t01kXlvrTLlZ2yuZn1xumgjZZ5pxeEXM4bwKI334VWogUl8Va1uVUNUQ9BAB-3iCagCjH4wt95aJPVFJJ_qjEMtw1081GKFin3zYNtoqqgxg340JRvJSA_3H144ni3rIb2QE_cKBoXz2VZuU9-Qz_seHiBlfRXyJ8J5j-tHkUXHyrH70KZAdFul_aLWpyqvPkOHKVnA1dYq4jdCcnchJjP0Xd8ijmK)," now available on DVD.

In this course, Professor Kenneth Calvert is your guide through the first four centuries of Christianity as he explains the remarkable ways the new faith transformed the Roman world.

Would you help support this course so we can make it available to millions of Americans for free? As a token of our appreciation for your support, we'll send you a copy of our beautiful DVD Box Set for any donations of $100 or more.
[](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=66139f92e44e4b94a908a6305fc9d659&_e=fUE7pILIHcujUnmdFwZNfuRa9dsbijl2ILYrZ18PHojmul-oEJS_qon2WCPHWhLtD0YA2Rt-wK-iNvSx5lJaeR1i9V1Di345UaBMFWTT2QmwExj_gLYigdk6sxvT7pYgnfJghyc8NLfBw-HZBnrSCPkIaAmNYyrr9LNz-4cAm-A-4GtNtmb1gLSSK0jM56adiDhnwNj_gSUMWAGZhNcY165fptls0tjFt1t01kXlvrTLlZ2yuZn1xumgjZZ5pxeEXM4bwKI334VWogUl8Va1uVUNUQ9BAB-3iCagCjH4wt-o6omY0sEhgxErutfJNhqdjmT_f9w1yntOvj8bpFFbl7gddRTpUckVMzVmBYpLM9pW1yZsO4DU8Fs8TJlTvPGweHw97-A18gR-Bk7cW9GyuDwnBUVGf21xdnTs05OmelUoJx87QF-ao417LLm_MSKT)

subject: Trump’s most recent rants
disclaimer_text: Paid for by The Pennsylvania Democratic Party
body:
| |
---
Peter,

Derek — It’s a
Thursday. The sun rose this morning and will set later today. And Elon
Musk accused me of treason. The more I hold him accountable for his
flagrant conflicts of interest, the more he lashes out.

It won’t stop me.

Elon took to social media earlier this week to share right-wing lies about
my leadership of Trump’s first impeachment, over, that’s right, Trump’s
effort to shakedown President Zelenskyy of Ukraine.

The more things change, the more they stay the same.

But it’s not my leadership of Trump’s impeachment that has Elon seething.
It’s my exposure of his massive conflicts of interest, and his potential
violations of the law against self-dealing.

You see, I demanded information from the head of the Office of Government
Ethics as to whether Elon was violating 18 U.S.C. Section 208, which makes
it a crime to participate in government decisions affecting your own
business interests, something Elon seems to be doing every day.

But before I could get an answer, the head of that office was fired. Along
with the firing of Inspector Generals, this action was designed to
facilitate the grift that is going on in the Trump Administration.

Nevertheless, I couldn’t help but be struck by the irony: accused of
treason just days after Donald Trump withdrew all military aid for our
ally, Ukraine, to bow down to Vladimir Putin and Russia. I told Elon that
if he was looking for someone betraying our country and its national
security interests, he needn’t look very far.

Now, these attacks aren’t new. I’ve had a target on my back for
years, Derek.

What is new is the authority that Elon Musk, Donald Trump, and countless
right-wing officials have to weaponize the government against me and
others.

Trump has given Musk unfettered access to millions of Americans’ data.
Kash Patel is in charge of the FBI and can investigate whomever he wants.
Pam Bondi can order the Justice Department to seek vengeance against any
and all of Trump’s rivals – including me. We have already seen the Justice
Department threaten Democratic officials for speaking out.

And we need to fight back.

We cannot let Elon’s lies go unanswered. And we certainly cannot turn our
backs on Ukraine and our fellow democracies around the world.

clean_body: [ ]Adam Schiff for Senate Derek — It’s a Thursday. The sun rose this morning and will set later today. And Elon Musk accused me of treason. The more I hold him accountable for his flagrant conflicts of interest, the more he lashes out. It won’t stop me. Elon took to social media earlier this week to share right-wing lies about my leadership of Trump’s first impeachment, over, that’s right, Trump’s effort to shakedown President Zelenskyy of Ukraine. The more things change, the more they stay the same. But it’s not my leadership of Trump’s impeachment that has Elon seething. It’s my exposure of his massive conflicts of interest, and his potential violations of the law against self-dealing. You see, I demanded information from the head of the Office of Government Ethics as to whether Elon was violating 18 U.S.C. Section 208, which makes it a crime to participate in government decisions affecting your own business interests, something Elon seems to be doing every day. But before I could get an answer, the head of that office was fired. Along with the firing of Inspector Generals, this action was designed to facilitate the grift that is going on in the Trump Administration. Nevertheless, I couldn’t help but be struck by the irony: accused of treason just days after Donald Trump withdrew all military aid for our ally, Ukraine, to bow down to Vladimir Putin and Russia. I told Elon that if he was looking for someone betraying our country and its national security interests, he needn’t look very far. Now, these attacks aren’t new. Patriot – I have spent some of the best years of my life fighting to save America from the radical left that wants to destroy it and sometimes, I’ve put that fight over the things I cherish the most.
I’ve missed birthdays, special occasions, and reunions...
I’ve come home completely exhausted from trying to secure victory in states far away from my home for **President Trump** and **our GOP majority**.
My dad served our country in the military, and he taught me how to love our country the way he does.
He still calls my mom his “bride” and I know that even when I don’t see him for months at a time, he understands the importance of **the work Early Vote Action does**.
My mom put everything she had into raising our family, and even today, she still puts everything she has into taking care of all of us.
I miss my family... But I would not change a single thing about the past few years, and **__[I will never give up this fight](http://email.email.freethinkerdaily.com/c/eJw8kD-PnDAQRz-N6RbZY8BQuEiCkFJckuaySmUZPNxaMf9sA-E-fQRabTlPT_o9jR5mZ_tDEvGVADysCQSA8C8EYI38t35_f_PHbflYltvOAU9O4NtT3eAlj53WU77etf7-GX4sb5H-239t7KXHY8aX_BxNcdDWnVTUiZEZaNZ3CUomMsap4IInD1mwimUGK0ML0aJuGTOlyYuqzTPRAy8SK4FCTjkVlEIFZQp9B2VZGF0W2HLKSUavobT3iPFhx7_ojbbuSLtpSJx8xDiHK6wh0ATsVo_pbkeP5jQINKi9O27bFPE8Nq3MNKppUOhVmG_hUD6oZ0ROeLPGQUX0A-F1Hw0jUKjRWUN4zdt79edzrZv7Ba938_qnB1jvS-sSL828W-dsKATJ6MeVfVZuEv4HAAD__7rCgwA)_._**
Someday, all of this is going to end. We will have transformed the Republican Party to always put America First. We will have successfully fought to drop unlawful voters from states’ voter rolls. We will have transformed voter demographics, and mobilized enough voters to save our country, once and for all.
That is, at least, _**my hope**_ , and **my dream**.
We ****_delivered Pennsylvania for President Trump_**. We were instrumental in _**revamping the RNC**_. We are so close to _**transforming New Jersey**_ into a red state that I can feel it.**
The support from patriots like you was instrumental in all of those victories, and we’re still not done. Without your support, we wouldn’t have accomplished any of what we’ve done so far.
I have given my life to this. If you believe this is still a cause worth fighting for, I hope you’ll chip in to help me keep doing it full time.
**__[Can I count on you to keep us in this fight](http://email.email.freethinkerdaily.com/c/eJw8kM2q2zAQRp9G3sXII1tyFl60DYEWbtvN7YVuxMQaJaLynyTbdZ--2IQs53DgOwx2o3d2a5j6zAAezkQGwMQnBjAn8Qvf39_Cdpru03RaBdDOGXx5qgu85L5FHKr5A_Hrv_h9ekv87_pzKV562kZ6yc_RnDp0fqfqkpmmBCxsm1FTqLIQXAklskcjJWJlJL-pWyWlOotSWYsSbIuFPXOeuQY4VFxwxTmcoc7BtlDX0mAt6Sa4YCU_hnIbiNLD9X8oGHR-y9uhy3zzSGmMR9iVwTVSOwfKV9cHMrvB4EoY_HZahkT7saA2Q6-HTlPQcTzFTYeonxEVE9c5dTpR6Ji42GQKBlL33hkmLp38_Y3qFKU54PFucfkRAOaP6eaz0Jhxdd67KBUr-f3I3iuXBv4HAAD__-gIg0I)_?_**

_Forever Fighting,_

Sylvester Turner's apparent cause of death detailed by police** ," Houston Chronicle's **Abby Church** -- "U.S. Rep.**Sylvester Turner** [died Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/ae926789-ac76-4093-9b3a-52cc094135ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at home from "enduring health complications," his family said in a statement posted on Turner's campaign website.

"Congressman Turner was the consummate public servant," the family's statement reads. "But to us, he was our beloved father, grandfather, sibling, and relative."

Turner's death was classified as an "apparent natural death," according to the Metropolitan Police Department in Washington, D.C.

A spokesperson with the department told the Houston Chronicle on Wednesday afternoon that fire, police and EMS officials received a medical call at 6:03 a.m. and responded to an apartment complex on the 800 block of New Jersey Avenue.

Once they arrived at the complex, officials found Turner dead.

In a statement Wednesday afternoon, Turner's office wrote the congressman "died peacefully."

"Congressman Turner dedicated his life to public service and the betterment of his community," the statement read, before chronicling his political career. "Throughout his career, he was known for his bipartisan leadership, dedication to his constituents and unwavering commitment to improving the lives of Houstonians."

Turner attended President **Donald Trump's** speech to Congress on Tuesday night, and afterward he defended Medicaid in a post on his X page, saying any cuts to the program would be an attack on the families Medicaid helps." "**Texas border city to Greg Abbott: Help us beat back cyberattack** ," San Antonio Express-News' **Marc Duvoisin** -- "Officials in the Texas border city of Mission say a cyberattack has stripped the city's computer network of its defenses and placed confidential health data and other records at risk. They're asking Gov. **Greg Abbott** for help.

Mayor **Norie Gonzalez Garza** [asked Abbott to declare a state of emergency](https://substack.com/redirect/c837e948-c48d-4dea-a303-ae60caf25843?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which could trigger financial aid and other assistance, Rio Grande Valley news media [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/f17f024b-bdc0-4235-9d58-82bd40dcc03f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

In a letter to the governor dated March 4, Garza said the "entire city computer server is at severe risk of a cyberattack that could release protected personal information, protected health information, civil and criminal records, and/or any and all other data held by the city of Mission and all departments within the city.

"I have determined that this incident is of such severity and magnitude that extraordinary measures must be taken," she wrote.

Abbott has yet to respond to the request.

Also this week, Garza issued a local disaster declaration.

City officials announced Feb. 28 that they had detected a cyberattack on a portion of the city's computer network. Officials said they immediately notified law enforcement and "began working with third-party experts to investigate and remediate the incident."

Some of the city's systems are being held offline to protect data.

Officials have revealed little about the nature of the attack, but local news media have reported that the Mission Police Department no longer could run license plates and driver's licenses through state databases.

"Please know that we are working to complete our investigation as quickly and thoroughly as we can. In the interim, our essential response services remain operational," a city new release said, referring to police and fire services." * **#TXLEGE**

"**Educators press Texas House to spend more per student** ," Dallas Morning News' **Philip Jankowski** -- "At a Thursday hearing at the Capitol, dozens of public school teachers and officials testified that a bill proposing $7.5 billion in school funding does not go far enough.

[House Bill 2](https://substack.com/redirect/0df9e528-39f7-493e-9466-91d1c2e747a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) proposes raising the per-student allotment by $220 to $6,360 a year, but teachers, administrators and advocates told the House Public Education Committee the increase falls short of meeting the needs of the state's school districts.

HB 2's proposed pay raises for teachers also were panned as inadequate.

"The pay teachers receive demonstrates the level of respect afforded to our children," said **Megan Holden** , a 10th grade English teacher at an Austin-area high school. "They are getting the message that Texas doesn't value them or their future."

HB 2 would devote 40% of the basic allotment to teacher pay.

The basic allotment would need to rise by $1,300 to keep up with inflation since 2019, when the Legislature last increased the payment, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The proposed $220 increase is also less than half of the $500 increase that was proposed in 2023 but died after Gov. Greg Abbott said he would veto any bill increasing school funding that did not create a program allowing public money to be spent on private schools.

HB 2 includes other mechanisms that provide money to public schools, but in more targeted fashions aimed at special education and pay boosts for high-performing teachers.

The House's proposal to raise teacher pay is part of a "Texas two step" Republicans have proposed in tandem with a voucher-style school choice proposal.

Rep.**Brad Buckley** , R-Salado, is the author of the school funding bill, the voucher proposal and another bill that would scale back the STAAR test and replace it with a different standardized testing system.

This week, the House Public Education Committee heard two days of testimony on the bills. Buckley, who chairs the committee, said he expected committee approval of the school finance bill March 18, sending it to the full House." "**SpaceX has lost another Starship, debris response effort begins** ," San Antonio Express-News'**Brandon Lingle** -- "After halting Monday's Starship launch attempt with seconds left in the countdown and [subsequent delays](https://substack.com/redirect/9d08ec09-e46a-4211-add7-629ec707361d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), SpaceX is trying again to launch the world's most powerful rocket from South Texas this evening. The launch window opens at 5:30 p.m.

Starship has been lost.

"We have lost contact with the ship," SpaceX spokesman **Dan Huot** said. "It's pretty obvious we're not going to continue the rest of the mission today." ...

A successful flight Thursday could have set the stage for SpaceX to attempt to land an upper-stage Starship back at its launch tower sometime this year.

On Friday, Musk laid out his current timeline for Starship development.

"We'll probably recover the ship sometime this year, and then we might be able to re-fly one, probably, with a fair bit of work, by the end of the year," he said on **Joe Rogan 's** podcast. "But it's going to take us many iterations before we can achieve rapid reusability."

Rapid re-use of the rocket is key to the company's plans for multiple Starship launches and for Musk's vision to get it to Mars.

"I think we'll achieve reusability of the ship this year, and I think we'll achieve rapid reusability of the whole stack -- ship and booster -- next year," Musk said. "This is the fundamental breakthrough required for life to become multiplanetary."

He said the company is "pretty close" to being able to quickly reuse the booster, but that it will take longer to get the upper-stage Starship to reach that milestone.

The biggest obstacle in the way of reusing Starship is developing a heat shield that survives the heating of reentry without requiring significant overhaul.

SpaceX also is seeking permission to launch and land as many as 25 Starships a year in South Texas. Its proposal also calls for possible Starship splashdowns in the Pacific Ocean around Hawaii. The FAA is still reviewing the request, which has drawn wide criticism from South Texans and residents of Hawaii." * **TEXANS IN DC**

"**House votes to censure Rep. Al Green for disrupting Trump speech** ," Texas Tribune's**Katharine Wilson** -- "The U.S. House of Representatives voted 224-198 to censure Rep. **Al Green** , D-Houston, for disrupting President Donald Trump's joint address to Congress on Tuesday.

Ten Democrats, none from Texas, voted to censure Green. Green voted "present." All Republicans, except four who did not vote, voted to censure Green.

Green [interrupted the president](https://substack.com/redirect/a34ec0e9-7b87-4600-9909-7b23a8079c90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) near the beginning of his joint address, standing and declaring that Trump had no mandate to cut Medicaid funding.

The representative was then escorted out of the House chamber by the Sergeant at Arms.

A censure is a formal vote of disapproval of a member's conduct by the U.S. House. There are no punishments associated with a censure, other than the official criticism from fellow members.

Immediately after being escorted out of the joint address, Green told reporters that he would accept punishment. The congressman said it was worth it to stand up to Trump's desire to cut Medicaid, Medicare and Social Security.

House Republicans passed a budget last week that opens the door for federal cuts, including to Medicaid, a health insurance program that helps low-income and disabled people.

Green is now the [28th House member](https://substack.com/redirect/8e20bbe1-2c69-4d40-bee3-9b67c9c19541?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to be censured in U.S. history. The House last censured Rep. Jamaal Bowman for [pulling a fire alarm](https://substack.com/redirect/103ce934-e6b0-4a2f-8502-8941b81e6631?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a congressional office building while Congress was in session.

The resolution orders that Green be present in the House chamber for the pronouncement of the censure.

As House Speaker **Mike Johnson** , R-Louisanna, read the final vote count, about 30 Democratic members stood with Green on the House floor, some of them singing.

Green, 77, has served in Congress since 2005." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/cd10bb99-efc8-49d3-a261-50dd93213482?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **TRUMP ADMINISTRATION**

"**South Texas immigration detention center with capacity for 2,400 people to reopen** ," Texas Tribune's**Alejandro Serrano** -- "A federal immigration detention center in South Texas previously used to hold families is being reopened by the Trump administration after former President **Joe Biden** closed it and ended the practice of detaining families.

The South Texas Family Residential Center in Dilley is among the largest in the country with a capacity to detain up to 2,400 people. The Biden administration closed it last summer because it was [reportedly far more expensive](https://substack.com/redirect/4c6e2c29-d3a3-42ec-a92d-24c3d5cae3ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to operate than other U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement facilities.

Shortly after taking office, Biden had stopped jailing families; the facility only held adults before it was closed.

On Wednesday, private prison corporation CoreCivic announced it had struck an agreement with Dilley city officials and ICE to resume operations at the facility -- and indicated that the Trump administration will resume detaining families.

"I can acknowledge that we anticipate housing families at this facility," a CoreCivic spokesperson said. He deferred further questions to ICE.

ICE officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Since it opened in 2015, the facility has been under [scrutiny from immigrants rights advocates](https://substack.com/redirect/eb7f453a-5ee4-4c3b-81e9-7b69413b59f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who question whether it is appropriate to jail families." "**Educators press Texas House to spend more per student** ," Dallas Morning News' **Philip Jankowski** -- "At a Thursday hearing at the Capitol, dozens of public school teachers and officials testified that a bill proposing $7.5 billion in school funding does not go far enough.

[House Bill 2](https://substack.com/redirect/3a5fb2d9-c083-4121-bc7a-d092abd46101?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) proposes raising the per-student allotment by $220 to $6,360 a year, but teachers, administrators and advocates told the House Public Education Committee the increase falls short of meeting the needs of the state's school districts.

HB 2's proposed pay raises for teachers also were panned as inadequate.

"The pay teachers receive demonstrates the level of respect afforded to our children," said **Megan Holden** , a 10th grade English teacher at an Austin-area high school. "They are getting the message that Texas doesn't value them or their future."

HB 2 would devote 40% of the basic allotment to teacher pay.

The basic allotment would need to rise by $1,300 to keep up with inflation since 2019, when the Legislature last increased the payment, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The proposed $220 increase is also less than half of the $500 increase that was proposed in 2023 but died after Gov. Greg Abbott said he would veto any bill increasing school funding that did not create a program allowing public money to be spent on private schools.

HB 2 includes other mechanisms that provide money to public schools, but in more targeted fashions aimed at special education and pay boosts for high-performing teachers.

The House's proposal to raise teacher pay is part of a "Texas two step" Republicans have proposed in tandem with a voucher-style school choice proposal.

Rep.**Brad Buckley** , R-Salado, is the author of the school funding bill, the voucher proposal and another bill that would scale back the STAAR test and replace it with a different standardized testing system.

This week, the House Public Education Committee heard two days of testimony on the bills. Buckley, who chairs the committee, said he expected committee approval of the school finance bill March 18, sending it to the full House." * **BUSINESS NEWS**

"**SpaceX has lost another Starship, debris response effort begins** ," San Antonio Express-News'**Brandon Lingle** -- "After halting Monday's Starship launch attempt with seconds left in the countdown and [subsequent delays](https://substack.com/redirect/1ddf4179-8a8d-4949-8451-a234bb6cb355?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), SpaceX is trying again to launch the world's most powerful rocket from South Texas this evening. The launch window opens at 5:30 p.m.

Starship has been lost.

"We have lost contact with the ship," SpaceX spokesman **Dan Huot** said. "It's pretty obvious we're not going to continue the rest of the mission today." ...

A successful flight Thursday could have set the stage for SpaceX to attempt to land an upper-stage Starship back at its launch tower sometime this year.

On Friday, Musk laid out his current timeline for Starship development.

"We'll probably recover the ship sometime this year, and then we might be able to re-fly one, probably, with a fair bit of work, by the end of the year," he said on **Joe Rogan 's** podcast. "But it's going to take us many iterations before we can achieve rapid reusability."

Rapid re-use of the rocket is key to the company's plans for multiple Starship launches and for Musk's vision to get it to Mars.

"I think we'll achieve reusability of the ship this year, and I think we'll achieve rapid reusability of the whole stack -- ship and booster -- next year," Musk said. "This is the fundamental breakthrough required for life to become multiplanetary."

He said the company is "pretty close" to being able to quickly reuse the booster, but that it will take longer to get the upper-stage Starship to reach that milestone.

The biggest obstacle in the way of reusing Starship is developing a heat shield that survives the heating of reentry without requiring significant overhaul.

SpaceX also is seeking permission to launch and land as many as 25 Starships a year in South Texas. Its proposal also calls for possible Starship splashdowns in the Pacific Ocean around Hawaii. The FAA is still reviewing the request, which has drawn wide criticism from South Texans and residents of Hawaii." * **TEXANS IN DC**

"**House votes to censure Rep. Al Green for disrupting Trump speech** ," Texas Tribune's**Katharine Wilson** -- "The U.S. House of Representatives voted 224-198 to censure Rep. **Al Green** , D-Houston, for disrupting President Donald Trump's joint address to Congress on Tuesday.

Ten Democrats, none from Texas, voted to censure Green. Green voted "present." All Republicans, except four who did not vote, voted to censure Green.

Green [interrupted the president](https://substack.com/redirect/6d3e042d-d1ed-44cb-8f36-0bc2c3f5d1e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) near the beginning of his joint address, standing and declaring that Trump had no mandate to cut Medicaid funding.

The representative was then escorted out of the House chamber by the Sergeant at Arms.

A censure is a formal vote of disapproval of a member's conduct by the U.S. House. There are no punishments associated with a censure, other than the official criticism from fellow members.

Immediately after being escorted out of the joint address, Green told reporters that he would accept punishment. The congressman said it was worth it to stand up to Trump's desire to cut Medicaid, Medicare and Social Security.

House Republicans passed a budget last week that opens the door for federal cuts, including to Medicaid, a health insurance program that helps low-income and disabled people.

Green is now the [28th House member](https://substack.com/redirect/aff1e6fc-fab3-4c68-8ab2-52c07182ec0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to be censured in U.S. history. The House last censured Rep. Jamaal Bowman for [pulling a fire alarm](https://substack.com/redirect/353db80a-b729-4eff-a6bd-e8d830bffcd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a congressional office building while Congress was in session.

The resolution orders that Green be present in the House chamber for the pronouncement of the censure.

As House Speaker **Mike Johnson** , R-Louisanna, read the final vote count, about 30 Democratic members stood with Green on the House floor, some of them singing.

Green, 77, has served in Congress since 2005." [Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/439e34f9-9d16-4c7c-83b9-bfdd8772e5bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **TRUMP ADMINISTRATION**

"**South Texas immigration detention center with capacity for 2,400 people to reopen** ," Texas Tribune's**Alejandro Serrano** -- "A federal immigration detention center in South Texas previously used to hold families is being reopened by the Trump administration after former President **Joe Biden** closed it and ended the practice of detaining families.

The South Texas Family Residential Center in Dilley is among the largest in the country with a capacity to detain up to 2,400 people. The Biden administration closed it last summer because it was [reportedly far more expensive](https://substack.com/redirect/a8b78331-dd30-4701-af8d-999f27edbefc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to operate than other U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement facilities.

Shortly after taking office, Biden had stopped jailing families; the facility only held adults before it was closed.

On Wednesday, private prison corporation CoreCivic announced it had struck an agreement with Dilley city officials and ICE to resume operations at the facility -- and indicated that the Trump administration will resume detaining families.

"I can acknowledge that we anticipate housing families at this facility," a CoreCivic spokesperson said. He deferred further questions to ICE.

ICE officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Since it opened in 2015, the facility has been under [scrutiny from immigrants rights advocates](https://substack.com/redirect/1ab6263f-f9df-42b8-9151-c10666eb44fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who question whether it is appropriate to jail families." Sylvester Turner's apparent cause of death detailed by police ," Houston Chronicle's Abby Church -- "U.S. Rep.Sylvester Turner at home from "enduring health complications," his family said in a statement posted on Turner's campaign website. "Congressman Turner was the consummate public servant," the family's statement reads. "But to us, he was our beloved father, grandfather, sibling, and relative." Turner's death was classified as an "apparent natural death," according to the Metropolitan Police Department in Washington, D.C. A spokesperson with the department told the Houston Chronicle on Wednesday afternoon that fire, police and EMS officials received a medical call at 6:03 a.m. and responded to an apartment complex on the 800 block of New Jersey Avenue. Once they arrived at the complex, officials found Turner dead. In a statement Wednesday afternoon, Turner's office wrote the congressman "died peacefully." "Congressman Turner dedicated his life to public service and the betterment of his community," the statement read, before chronicling his political career. "Throughout his career, he was known for his bipartisan leadership, dedication to his constituents and unwavering commitment to improving the lives of Houstonians." Turner attended President Donald Trump's speech to Congress on Tuesday night, and afterward he defended Medicaid in a post on his X page, saying any cuts to the program would be an attack on the families Medicaid helps." ($) "Texas border city to Greg Abbott: Help us beat back cyberattack ," San Antonio Express-News' Marc Duvoisin -- "Officials in the Texas border city of Mission say a cyberattack has stripped the city's computer network of its defenses and placed confidential health data and other records at risk. They're asking Gov. Greg Abbott for help. Mayor Norie Gonzalez Garza , which could trigger financial aid and other assistance, Rio Grande Valley news media . In a letter to the governor dated March 4, Garza said the "entire city computer server is at severe risk of a cyberattack that could release protected personal information, protected health information, civil and criminal records, and/or any and all other data held by the city of Mission and all departments within the city. "I have determined that this incident is of such severity and magnitude that extraordinary measures must be taken," she wrote. Abbott has yet to respond to the request. Also this week, Garza issued a local disaster declaration. City officials announced Feb. 28 that they had detected a cyberattack on a portion of the city's computer network. Officials said they immediately notified law enforcement and "began working with third-party experts to investigate and remediate the incident." Some of the city's systems are being held offline to protect data. Officials have revealed little about the nature of the attack, but local news media have reported that the Mission Police Department no longer could run license plates and driver's licenses through state databases. "Please know that we are working to complete our investigation as quickly and thoroughly as we can. In the interim, our essential response services remain operational," a city new release said, referring to police and fire services." ($) #TXLEGE "Educators press Texas House to spend more per student ," Dallas Morning News' Philip Jankowski -- "At a Thursday hearing at the Capitol, dozens of public school teachers and officials testified that a bill proposing $7.5 billion in school funding does not go far enough. proposes raising the per-student allotment by $220 to $6,360 a year, but teachers, administrators and advocates told the House Public Education Committee the increase falls short of meeting the needs of the state's school districts. HB 2's proposed pay raises for teachers also were panned as inadequate. "The pay teachers receive demonstrates the level of respect afforded to our children," said Megan Holden , a 10th grade English teacher at an Austin-area high school. "They are getting the message that Texas doesn't value them or their future." HB 2 would devote 40% of the basic allotment to teacher pay. The basic allotment would need to rise by $1,300 to keep up with inflation since 2019, when the Legislature last increased the payment, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The proposed $220 increase is also less than half of the $500 increase that was proposed in 2023 but died after Gov. Greg Abbott said he would veto any bill increasing school funding that did not create a program allowing public money to be spent on private schools. HB 2 includes other mechanisms that provide money to public schools, but in more targeted fashions aimed at special education and pay boosts for high-performing teachers. The House's proposal to raise teacher pay is part of a "Texas two step" Republicans have proposed in tandem with a voucher-style school choice proposal. Rep.Brad Buckley , R-Salado, is the author of the school funding bill, the voucher proposal and another bill that would scale back the STAAR test and replace it with a different standardized testing system. This week, the House Public Education Committee heard two days of testimony on the bills. Buckley, who chairs the committee, said he expected committee approval of the school finance bill March 18, sending it to the full House." ($) BUSINESS NEWS "SpaceX has lost another Starship, debris response effort begins ," San Antonio Express-News'Brandon Lingle -- "After halting Monday's Starship launch attempt with seconds left in the countdown and , SpaceX is trying again to launch the world's most powerful rocket from South Texas this evening. The launch window opens at 5:30 p.m. Starship has been lost. "We have lost contact with the ship," SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. "It's pretty obvious we're not going to continue the rest of the mission today." ... A successful flight Thursday could have set the stage for SpaceX to attempt to land an upper-stage Starship back at its launch tower sometime this year. On Friday, Musk laid out his current timeline for Starship development. "We'll probably recover the ship sometime this year, and then we might be able to re-fly one, probably, with a fair bit of work, by the end of the year," he said on Joe Rogan 's podcast. "But it's going to take us many iterations before we can achieve rapid reusability." Rapid re-use of the rocket is key to the company's plans for multiple Starship launches and for Musk's vision to get it to Mars. "I think we'll achieve reusability of the ship this year, and I think we'll achieve rapid reusability of the whole stack -- ship and booster -- next year," Musk said. "This is the fundamental breakthrough required for life to become multiplanetary." He said the company is "pretty close" to being able to quickly reuse the booster, but that it will take longer to get the upper-stage Starship to reach that milestone. The biggest obstacle in the way of reusing Starship is developing a heat shield that survives the heating of reentry without requiring significant overhaul. SpaceX also is seeking permission to launch and land as many as 25 Starships a year in South Texas. Its proposal also calls for possible Starship splashdowns in the Pacific Ocean around Hawaii. The FAA is still reviewing the request, which has drawn wide criticism from South Texans and residents of Hawaii." ($) TEXANS IN DC "House votes to censure Rep. Al Green for disrupting Trump speech ," Texas Tribune'sKatharine Wilson -- "The U.S. House of Representatives voted 224-198 to censure Rep. Al Green , D-Houston, for disrupting President Donald Trump's joint address to Congress on Tuesday. Ten Democrats, none from Texas, voted to censure Green. Green voted "present." All Republicans, except four who did not vote, voted to censure Green. Green near the beginning of his joint address, standing and declaring that Trump had no mandate to cut Medicaid funding. The representative was then escorted out of the House chamber by the Sergeant at Arms. A censure is a formal vote of disapproval of a member's conduct by the U.S. House. There are no punishments associated with a censure, other than the official criticism from fellow members. Immediately after being escorted out of the joint address, Green told reporters that he would accept punishment. The congressman said it was worth it to stand up to Trump's desire to cut Medicaid, Medicare and Social Security. House Republicans passed a budget last week that opens the door for federal cuts, including to Medicaid, a health insurance program that helps low-income and disabled people. Green is now the to be censured in U.S. history. The House last censured Rep. Jamaal Bowman for in a congressional office building while Congress was in session. The resolution orders that Green be present in the House chamber for the pronouncement of the censure. As House Speaker Mike Johnson , R-Louisanna, read the final vote count, about 30 Democratic members stood with Green on the House floor, some of them singing. Green, 77, has served in Congress since 2005." TRUMP ADMINISTRATION "South Texas immigration detention center with capacity for 2,400 people to reopen ," Texas Tribune'sAlejandro Serrano -- "A federal immigration detention center in South Texas previously used to hold families is being reopened by the Trump administration after former President Joe Biden closed it and ended the practice of detaining families. The South Texas Family Residential Center in Dilley is among the largest in the country with a capacity to detain up to 2,400 people. The Biden administration closed it last summer because it was to operate than other U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement facilities. Shortly after taking office, Biden had stopped jailing families; the facility only held adults before it was closed. On Wednesday, private prison corporation CoreCivic announced it had struck an agreement with Dilley city officials and ICE to resume operations at the facility -- and indicated that the Trump administration will resume detaining families. "I can acknowledge that we anticipate housing families at this facility," a CoreCivic spokesperson said. He deferred further questions to ICE. ICE officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Since it opened in 2015, the facility has been under who question whether it is appropriate to jail families." “**Educators press Texas House to spend more per student** ,” Dallas Morning News' **Philip Jankowski** — “At a Thursday hearing at the Capitol, dozens of public school teachers and officials testified that a bill proposing $7.5 billion in school funding does not go far enough.

[House Bill 2](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.y1qQg7vX491TJbzrGLYTuEYT0yv_aZw1IceJac_-o0Y-UGIWKkPTFm9Kz5DRdvb_-aYU7NLaOywMgY5yceksY4shW88ol0Lq3V2TMt6hCBtEkDk2kuBbd7iis9d2eJ100crfEathp5UfUHswM-AEIXvnOy7AmOMQ3s1A565qapjtR8elL0oAoGn1NvQehYnNYNkoAOJf2OVxoRc4OV7KZ2Nodm_PFTnS0VhoVOYin2idOTh0lIyoZG-axHpI5oLrqhCHuYl27jhVEUbqnXL2Fbivu_x5ryq30YAR-VXnwJ0FQ-LIdIrAqsjSNX0ojJZSd_Ixoo1B1T3zOADYlxG2FYGXYEUN1Ph5uWcP-K174yLQZ3J06g3Lub333guUdyMRU3iukZZbbwSDvuWx1K0aZIUiwor_Cu_hw-jg_y_iWjev0052m0I_4o6mAZ4NNhxk6IQnvINnfN_LLMcjl9k9NlUBr6yu3rqT2PRqAnc1YFRCPjUdHXcGULrG_XBAmnrnxHLkGkchuM7VYbu2H2L5hQ/4el/3ZftL4-zTpehIj6nKr7fXQ/h19/h001.nFSFZyb8cGZNBm7U1xDo5u6DXFQ3HUd1n1IhZhRPX44) proposes raising the per-student allotment by $220 to $6,360 a year, but teachers, administrators and advocates told the House Public Education Committee the increase falls short of meeting the needs of the state’s school districts.

“The pay teachers receive demonstrates the level of respect afforded to our children,” said **Megan Holden** , a 10th grade English teacher at an Austin-area high school. “They are getting the message that Texas doesn’t value them or their future.”

Greg Abbott said he would veto any bill increasing school funding that did not create a program allowing public money to be spent on private schools.

HB 2 includes other mechanisms that provide money to public schools, but in more targeted fashions aimed at special education and pay boosts for high-performing teachers.

The House’s proposal to raise teacher pay is part of a “Texas two step” Republicans have proposed in tandem with a voucher-style school choice proposal.

"We have lost contact with the ship," SpaceX spokesman **Dan Huot** said. "It’s pretty obvious we’re not going to continue the rest of the mission today.” ...

A successful flight Thursday could have set the stage for SpaceX to attempt to land an upper-stage Starship back at its launch tower sometime this year.

On Friday, Musk laid out his current timeline for Starship development.

“We’ll probably recover the ship sometime this year, and then we might be able to re-fly one, probably, with a fair bit of work, by the end of the year,” he said on **Joe Rogan’s** podcast. “But it’s going to take us many iterations before we can achieve rapid reusability.”

Rapid re-use of the rocket is key to the company’s plans for multiple Starship launches and for Musk’s vision to get it to Mars.

“I think we’ll achieve reusability of the ship this year, and I think we’ll achieve rapid reusability of the whole stack — ship and booster — next year,” Musk said. “This is the fundamental breakthrough required for life to become multiplanetary.”

He said the company is “pretty close” to being able to quickly reuse the booster, but that it will take longer to get the upper-stage Starship to reach that milestone.

The biggest obstacle in the way of reusing Starship is developing a heat shield that survives the heating of reentry without requiring significant overhaul.

SpaceX also is seeking permission to launch and land as many as 25 Starships a year in South Texas. Its proposal also calls for possible Starship splashdowns in the Pacific Ocean around Hawaii. The FAA is still reviewing the request, which has drawn wide criticism from South Texans and residents of Hawaii." Turner's death was classified as an “apparent natural death,” according to the Metropolitan Police Department in Washington, D.C. A spokesperson with the department told the Houston Chronicle on Wednesday afternoon that fire, police and EMS officials received a medical call at 6:03 a.m. and responded to an apartment complex on the 800 block of New Jersey Avenue. They're asking Gov. Greg Abbott for help. Mayor Norie Gonzalez Garza , which could trigger financial aid and other assistance, Rio Grande Valley news media . In a letter to the governor dated March 4, Garza said the "entire city computer server is at severe risk of a cyberattack that could release protected personal information, protected health information, civil and criminal records, and/or any and all other data held by the city of Mission and all departments within the city. “I have determined that this incident is of such severity and magnitude that extraordinary measures must be taken,” she wrote. Abbott has yet to respond to the request. Also this week, Garza issued a local disaster declaration. City officials announced Feb. 28 that they had detected a cyberattack on a portion of the city's computer network. Officials said they immediately notified law enforcement and "began working with third-party experts to investigate and remediate the incident." Some of the city’s systems are being held offline to protect data. Officials have revealed little about the nature of the attack, but local news media have reported that the Mission Police Department no longer could run license plates and driver’s licenses through state databases. “Please know that we are working to complete our investigation as quickly and thoroughly as we can. HB 2’s proposed pay raises for teachers also were panned as inadequate. “The pay teachers receive demonstrates the level of respect afforded to our children,” said Megan Holden , a 10th grade English teacher at an Austin-area high school. “They are getting the message that Texas doesn’t value them or their future.” HB 2 would devote 40% of the basic allotment to teacher pay. The basic allotment would need to rise by $1,300 to keep up with inflation since 2019, when the Legislature last increased the payment, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The proposed $220 increase is also less than half of the $500 increase that was proposed in 2023 but died after Gov. Greg Abbott said he would veto any bill increasing school funding that did not create a program allowing public money to be spent on private schools. HB 2 includes other mechanisms that provide money to public schools, but in more targeted fashions aimed at special education and pay boosts for high-performing teachers. The House’s proposal to raise teacher pay is part of a “Texas two step” Republicans have proposed in tandem with a voucher-style school choice proposal. Rep.Brad Buckley , R-Salado, is the author of the school funding bill, the voucher proposal and another bill that would scale back the STAAR test and replace it with a different standardized testing system. This week, the House Public Education Committee heard two days of testimony on the bills. Buckley, who chairs the committee, said he expected committee approval of the school finance bill March 18, sending it to the full House." A successful flight Thursday could have set the stage for SpaceX to attempt to land an upper-stage Starship back at its launch tower sometime this year. On Friday, Musk laid out his current timeline for Starship development. “We’ll probably recover the ship sometime this year, and then we might be able to re-fly one, probably, with a fair bit of work, by the end of the year,” he said on Joe Rogan’s podcast. “But it’s going to take us many iterations before we can achieve rapid reusability.” Rapid re-use of the rocket is key to the company’s plans for multiple Starship launches and for Musk’s vision to get it to Mars. “I think we’ll achieve reusability of the ship this year, and I think we’ll achieve rapid reusability of the whole stack — ship and booster — next year,” Musk said. “This is the fundamental breakthrough required for life to become multiplanetary.” He said the company is “pretty close” to being able to quickly reuse the booster, but that it will take longer to get the upper-stage Starship to reach that milestone. The biggest obstacle in the way of reusing Starship is developing a heat shield that survives the heating of reentry without requiring significant overhaul. SpaceX also is seeking permission to launch and land as many as 25 Starships a year in South Texas. Its proposal also calls for possible Starship splashdowns in the Pacific Ocean around Hawaii. Green near the beginning of his joint address, standing and declaring that Trump had no mandate to cut Medicaid funding. The representative was then escorted out of the House chamber by the Sergeant at Arms. A censure is a formal vote of disapproval of a member’s conduct by the U.S. House. There are no punishments associated with a censure, other than the official criticism from fellow members. Immediately after being escorted out of the joint address, Green told reporters that he would accept punishment. The congressman said it was worth it to stand up to Trump’s desire to cut Medicaid, Medicare and Social Security. House Republicans passed a budget last week that opens the door for federal cuts, including to Medicaid, a health insurance program that helps low-income and disabled people. # **Pennsylvania Needs More Teachers!**
_Pennsylvania 's Student Teacher Stipend Program, originally introduced by Senator Hughes, is helping student teachers pay their bills while they complete their unpaid, student teaching requirement_ Senator Hughes went to West Philly High School to celebrate Philadelphia student teachers who have been selected to receive $10,000 to support them during their student teaching requirement. The stipends were awarded through Pennsylvania's new [Student Teacher Support Program](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169632.172252.34&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13758). Senator Hughes introduced the Student Teacher Support Program with his Republican colleague back in 2023 and has fought for the past two years to get money in the hands of our future teachers. **Pennsylvania was able to provide a stipend to over 2,000 student teachers for the 24-25 school year.** Now, Senator Hughes is working with the Governor and his colleagues in the Senate and House to provide stipends to even [more student teachers for the 25-26 school year.](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169632.172252.34&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13758) He wants the program to have enough funding to provide every student teacher with a stipend to support their journey to becoming a certified Pennsylvania teacher.
* * *
**Pennsylvania's Teacher Shortage Crisis ** The Student Teacher Support Program was created to help address Pennsylvania's teacher shortage crisis. In Philadelphia, school officials struggle to fill about 2,000 vacancies a year. Students, teachers, and parents know firsthand, when schools don't have sufficient, well-trained, and experienced teachers, there can be a number of negative repercussions including:
* Larger class sizes
* Lower student achievement
* Teacher burnout
* Less access to extracurricular activities

Senator Hughes explained, "This program is an opportunity to breathe hope and curiosity into our children through our educators and fix the system to bring more quality and diverse teachers into our schools."
* * *
**Applications are OPEN NOW for Student Teacher Stipends for the 25-26 School Year** Individuals who will be student teaching in the 25-26 school year can [apply for a student teacher stipend today on the PHEAA website.](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169632.172252.34&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13758) [](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169632.172252.34&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13759) If you or someone you know will be student teaching in the next school year, make a plan for you or them to get an application in to access funding that is meant to support future teachers. **Stipends will be awarded on a first come, first serve basis.** **Applicants can apply online at[PHEAA.ORG/STUDENTTEACHER](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169632.172252.34&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13758)** [](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169632.172252.34&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13759)

Hop on at 9pm ET on Rumble** | [](https://laroucheorganization.nationbuilder.com/r?u=gFB7Tylx1fPa2jOHrKCBPpoPlQNzvk59soiRH3zWGYQy2CE5i2Cw4SX9hOpKJ0gmmynDPJ26D5j2IzDoi7jSVJls1ZRhdo9YRBvNUwBZaU4&e=8fa7b86c85d8b09f0015ebe544605791&utm_source=laroucheorganization&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=20250306_fireside_chat&n=3 "Listen on Rumble") [Listen on Rumble](https://laroucheorganization.nationbuilder.com/r?u=gFB7Tylx1fPa2jOHrKCBPpoPlQNzvk59soiRH3zWGYQy2CE5i2Cw4SX9hOpKJ0gmmynDPJ26D5j2IzDoi7jSVJls1ZRhdo9YRBvNUwBZaU4&e=8fa7b86c85d8b09f0015ebe544605791&utm_source=laroucheorganization&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=20250306_fireside_chat&n=3)

+13092053325,,83226412240# US

Webinar ID: 832 2641 2240**
A series of political earthquakes seem to be coming every day, especially since Zelenskyy’s ill-fated meeting with President Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance, where Trump had said flatly to the Ukrainian dictator, “You are gambling with World War III.”
Since that meeting, President Trump has canceled all military aid to Ukraine, a decision which has panicked the trans-Atlantic establishment in Europe who are dead set against any kind of peace talks with Russia, and are now doubling down on militarizing their countries. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has called for €800 billion to “rearm Europe,” which cannot possibly work given the fragile budgets of the European economies.
A shattering of the old order—based on Unipolar dominance, endless wars, and sanctions—is clearly coming to an end. However, those that are in most panic are the British imperial elites, who have been the leading actors in manipulating great powers to fight each other since the untimely death of President Franklin Roosevelt.
The conservative British imperialist David Starkey, known for his racist, pro-colonialist views, revealed his view of the Trump/Zelenskyy dust-up in a recent interview given on March 2nd.
Starkey said, “The world in which we thought we lived, in which most of my lifetime we’ve lived, which is a world of the so-called ‘Rules-Based International System’—RUBIS—has shattered.... Exactly three years ago, on the day that Putin invaded, I predicted the end of RUBIS. I predicted the fact that we are going to move into a world which looks very much like the terrible world outlawed by George Orwell in 1984, in which there are great, permanent blocs of the world. He outlined Oceania, which is ourselves and America; Eurasia, which is, essentially, an enlarged Soviet Union; with an uneasy southern hemisphere. And it’s something like that.
“We now have the combined power of Russia and China, we have the so-called BRICS, with India, with South Africa, with Brazil. We have the Anglosphere, all now in extraordinary competition with one another. We’ve moved back from that world of the United Nations, into something like 19th century great power politics.... We’re back in the world of Palmerston.”
Is the intention by the British Empire to keep the world divided by “great power” blocs, who are constantly at odds with one another in a new, 21st Century “Great Game”?
That is not how we view a “multipolar” world order, which would be more correctly identified as “polyphonic,” where nations work together for the common good of each other, and whereby a new, security and development architecture can be established among equal, sovereign nation-states. That coheres with Chinese President Xi Jinping’s Global Security Initiative, Global Development Initiative, and Global Civilization Initiative, along with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s proposal for a joint European security architecture in a speech he gave to the Federal Security Service of Russia (FSB) on Feb. 27th.
The old order is collapsing, but let us not collapse with it.
****
**Have Fun,**
Dennis Speed

**Dear Subscribers, Followers, Friends, and Foes,**
This isn't my typical Substack article where I disseminate critical or timely information on human rights. Instead, it's an ask so I can learn critical information from you.
I've spent decades advocating for justice, human rights, and policies that serve the people. But advocacy isn't only about speaking--_it 's more importantly about listening_.
I want to better understand what matters most to you and how I can be a more effective advocate for the issues you care about? **To do that, I 've partnered with Oak on a short, anonymous survey.**
[Take Qasim's Survey](https://substack.com/redirect/c904733b-fe1d-4146-94e6-be3eecd9ff47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This survey is about action. It's about understanding how you engage with the causes you care about--what drives you, what challenges you face, and what tools or content may help you take action more effectively. Your insights will shape how I approach my work, ensuring that my content and advocacy efforts are truly aligned with your needs.
💡 **Why take 7 minutes to fill this out? Three important reasons:**
1. **It 's completely anonymous. **This is solely to help me be a better advocate. No personal information is collected, and nothing is sold for marketing.
2. **Your voice helps shape the conversation.** The more I understand what moves you, the better I can advocate for the issues you care about.
3. **You help build something bigger.** This is truly about all of us working toward meaningful change together. Your insights help me do that.

And that's why your time and perspective are deeply valuable to me. It's also why you'll notice there's no link or button to share or subscribe to Let's Address This. This post is truly about one thing and one thing only: **me learning from you.**
[ Take Qasim's Survey](https://substack.com/redirect/c904733b-fe1d-4146-94e6-be3eecd9ff47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
So, if you have a few minutes, I'd love to hear from you. Thank you for being part of this journey. And never hesitate to reach out directly.
**Let 's keep building together.**
**Sincerely,**
**Qasim**

| | Folks, **Alabama’s congressional map is at stake in a federal trial** that wil decide if the state will keep the new court-created district that led to the election of a second Black representative. From the AP: "_A three-judge panel will decide whether congressional lines drawn by state lawmakers diluted the voting power of Black residents. The same panel already ruled against Alabama in pre-trial decisions that reshaped the 2nd Congressional District before Rep. Shomari Figures won election in November, giving Alabama two Black representatives in its delegation for the first time in history._ " **The state of Alabama is seeking to reinstate the maps created by the suppressive state legislature.** This case began in 2021 when Black voters and civil rights groups filed lawsuits over Alabama’s state-drawn congressional map they said disenfranchised Black voters. **[Team, we have to make sure voters everywhere know about this case to protect fair maps in court. subject: They want to cut Medicaid

| Dear Peter:

Victoria Ellen Bruce is my mom’s younger sister. She loved to play bid wiz, to hear and tell a good joke, and she never saw a purse she didn’t need. “Oooh, girl, give it here,” she’d say on the regular.

My Aunt Vicki died last year.

This loss has been deep and painful for my family. My mother grieves every day. She thinks about her, talks about her, cries over her. It is so hard to lose your younger sibling, especially one so full of life, love, hope and faith. That was Aunt Vicki.

She was strong.

She lived with multiple sclerosis for most of her adult life. We would go to events and she would just fall. After too many of these episodes, she went to the doctor and was diagnosed with this debilitating and incurable disease. We were filled with disbelief and sadness, but showed us faith. The falls became more frequent. A walker led to a wheelchair, a scooter and eventually a bed at a long-term residential facility.

My Aunt had the best caregiver care in my grandmother (a nurse) and my mom (a Leo). They both fought hard against the system.

In January, my mom came to Washington to check on me, make eye contact with Republicans so they know I am her child, and finally watch me get sworn in. Remember the Speaker drama when I tried to get sworn in the first time???

Before she left, she gave me an article to read about the national nursing home ombudsmen program. The article highlighted Melinda Lundey. Her job is to visit assisted living facilities and residential care homes to make sure the patients – our family members – are not abused. I read about a patient who died after mistaking cleaning chemicals for juice. In some facilities, the elderly or patients with disabilities have gone unwashed for over a year, do not get their teeth brushed regularly, or are made to sleep overnight in soiled or soaked briefs.

Even with my mother's dogged and formidable advocacy, Aunt Vicki was neglected by the system. As the MS worsened, she required more consistent and observant care. Her health and safety became increasingly compromised because she did not get what she deserved. The disease eventually made her completely bedridden. Staying in the same place in bed for hours at a time without being moved brought bed sores. Without proper care, the bed sores turned into open wounds. My mother would ride the nursing home administrators. She wrote letters, made calls, showed up, and chewed people out. She stayed in their asses. The care would get better and then it would backslide. That is the life of a caregiver.

I can still recount my mother telling me about the first time she saw Vicki's wounds. She said, "it was so deep, I could see to the bone."

Most people who live in these facilities are on Medicaid. The program keeps them alive. It pays for their care, housing AND for the ombudsmen – of which there are too few.

Annual federal funding for this important nationwide ombudsmen program was $22 million in 2023 and 2024, well below the recommended ombudsmen-per-bed ratios. In 2023, there were 202,894 long-term care facility complaints and only 5,014 ombudsmen staff and representatives available to investigate.

That is a disgrace.

Now, Republicans are slashing Medicaid and it is likely they will get rid of this very critical program.

For many patients, their only advocate and hope are people like Melinda Lundey. Without people like her, many of our loved ones will die.

Aunt Vicki loved to get a phone call from her niece. We would talk, laugh and share stories. Eventually, she would tell me about some grievance with the nursing home and then she would say how grateful she was grateful for my mother. We should all be so lucky to have a caregiver as dedicated as my mom.

I loved Aunt Vicki so much and I know that she deserved better care from Medicaid than she got. So many deserve better.

It is unconscionable to cut Medicaid.

Speaker Johnson is lying when he says the program will not be touched – every safety net program will be slashed in order to fun the $4.5 trillion Billionaire Boys Club tax cut that Republicans just passed, including Medicaid.

We cannot stand for this.

Caregivers like my mom and patients like my aunt deserve a Medicaid program that is properly resourced so that it works, but it can’t work if workers are fired, funding is slashed, and programs are cut.

We cannot stand for this.

Share your story. We can breathe life into Medicaid with our stories, so that everyone understands how vital it is to our families and to the people we love.

We must fight to protect and fix Medicaid. It keeps people alive.

He can’t afford to lose more than one vote to pass any Republican policies.
That’s why Sean Spicer is giving him some advice: He should tie conditions to California wildfire relief to other Republican initiatives and hopefully *FORCE* members of the California delegation to support Trump’s policies.
These “strings” could include things like:
1️⃣ Demanding that California loosen our clean air standards and repeal pro-electric vehicle policies;
2️⃣ Ordering that we roll back voting rights in our state;
3️⃣ Backing Trump legislative initiatives.

I am doing everything I can to save our country.
| [View in Web Browser](https://email.email.america1stwarroom.com/c/eJw8kE1v4jAQhn-NfSOyZ_yBDz4sy3qlIlVUoCrtzYkTcBWTkIRE_PsKSrnOPDPvo9enron11RK9IgDHGAYCQPAPATh_zKm_fKXN_4XIcbs4q9ckb1v4-0AneMKn0q8_33aHQu6nIfGT6xTmE3_i47WrnvAjNKuSj81tqtc0WKwDE7SyXAuO3Ei5pEcrUWmpCiUMCm6MDAUKJiu1VAFYYWoaLTCQDJlmKAFMpkUtJDcKea0QJBLB7jmZT1UfS8-HcfZ937YpK9tEG3scx264izkCbu7b7HQpm-oy_JyVbSLgHsoE3ETACb_K1fsm3-0JuntpuG5ftn4fZvhHexu6OTZNHJQmgh1-39DJwncAAAD__7MXbH8)

Patriot – I have spent some of the best years of my life fighting to save America from the radical left that wants to destroy it and sometimes, I’ve put that fight over the things I cherish the most.
I’ve missed birthdays, special occasions, and reunions...
I’ve come home completely exhausted from trying to secure victory in states far away from my home for **President Trump** and **our GOP majority**.
My dad served our country in the military, and he taught me how to love our country the way he does.
He still calls my mom his “bride” and I know that even when I don’t see him for months at a time, he understands the importance of **the work Early Vote Action does**.
My mom put everything she had into raising our family, and even today, she still puts everything she has into taking care of all of us.
I miss my family... But I would not change a single thing about the past few years, and **__[I will never give up this fight](https://email.email.america1stwarroom.com/c/eJw8jk-vnCAUxT8N7sbAvYDPBYu2xi6aNG3axWs3BgHf0Ig64J_47RsmZpbn3F_u-emwjH44Fak-E4C7t4kAEPxEAB5_jhC3f-Hb1xt_xx-3h_weRL7Clwvd4QVPRjd_f_766MXvPQU2tYvE95298PVc3Au-RksXtB9zWzWFVThYygunWMUZslqIt-KuWG_Y8GbRUVuxQcteMFFTHIzlgFrSwiugICjSiqIAqMuKD1ywWiIbJIJAwulzp9TBRW80S-uhY5znUJo5FKO6r-uSnmItgTY5s0VXHn6KzmaCQOt0HM_bPq8uh113dp66OXQudmm5pbOLqbssRP6C7baGLs1bNI5gM5mRgMxVcNZvgWDTx6tZXcz5iKyIyi6HH0efZEU4_XhKZ8Vdwf8AAAD__5XFgU8)_._**
Someday, all of this is going to end. We will have transformed the Republican Party to always put America First. We will have successfully fought to drop unlawful voters from states’ voter rolls. We will have transformed voter demographics, and mobilized enough voters to save our country, once and for all.
That is, at least, _**my hope**_ , and **my dream**.
We **_delivered Pennsylvania for President Trump_**. We were instrumental in _**revamping the RNC**_. We are so close to _**transforming New Jersey**_ into a red state that I can feel it.
The support from patriots like you was instrumental in all of those victories, and we’re still not done. Without your support, we wouldn’t have accomplished any of what we’ve done so far.
I have given my life to this. If you believe this is still a cause worth fighting for, I hope you’ll chip in to help me keep doing it full time.
**__[Can I count on you to keep us in this fight](https://email.email.america1stwarroom.com/c/eJw8jk-vnCAUxT8N7sbAvYDPBYu2xi6aNG3axWs3BgHf0Ig64J_47RsmZpbn3F_u-emwjH44Fak-E4C7t4kAEPxEAB5_jhC3f-Hb1xt_xx-3h_weRL7Clwvd4QVPRjd_f_766MXvPQU2tYvE95298PVc3Au-RksXtB9zWzWFVThYygunWMUZslqIt-KuWG_Y8GbRUVuxQcteMFFTHIzlgFrSwiugICjSiqIAqMuKD1ywWiIbJIJAwulzp9TBRW80S-uhY5znUJo5FKO6r-uSnmItgTY5s0VXHn6KzmaCQOt0HM_bPq8uh113dp66OXQudmm5pbOLqbssRP6C7baGLs1bNI5gM5mRgMxVcNZvgWDTx6tZXcz5iKyIyi6HH0efZEU4_XhKZ8Vdwf8AAAD__5XFgU8)_?_**

_Forever Fighting,_

**Scott Presler** Founder, Early Vote Action

| | Dear Friend,

Learning about how early Christians worshipped and prayed, faced persecution and hardship, and settled theological disputes enriches our understanding of the faith. These lessons are especially important today, as Christians face increasing opposition from the culture.

subject: A ticking time-bomb set by Joe Biden and Kamala Harris
body:
It isn’t rocket-science. It’s basic math.

| |
---
| | It isn’t rocket-science. It’s basic math.
---
| |
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zrhj029v347dgucqsu8o7sfrbtmp5f3adugavgko_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cpgmaoj1cth2bs)
---
| | **“****A disproportionate number of illegal immigrants go to blue states, they amplify the effect of a blue state vote. My understanding is that Democrats would lose approximately 20 seats in the house if illegals were not counted in census. And that’s also 20 less electoral votes for president.**** ** **So, illegals absolutely do impact who controls the House and the presidency.”****~** Elon Musk
---
| | Fellow Conservative,Elon Musk is right. It isn’t rocket-science. It’s basic math. It’s also a ticking time-bomb set by Joe Biden and Kamala Harris – in the form of 11.5 million illegals entering our country on their watch – one which will explode shortly after President Trump leaves office in 2029.While you and I have no doubt President Trump will deliver on his promise to secure the border, this threat will not go away. The truth is, without immediate action, these illegal aliens will be counted in the U.S. Census, which determines both the apportionment of seats in the House of Representatives _and_ the number of electoral votes given to each state. Whether they came because, four years ago, Kamala Harris and Joe Biden prompted them to “surge to the border” for asylum or because of blue-states offering sanctuary status, “free” health care, “free” cell phones, “free” housing, and “free” college...it doesn’t matter. The result is the same.Your vote is _already_ being **watered down** in Congress. Your vote is _already_ being **watered down** in the Electoral College.And every day reports are popping up of non-citizens, illegal aliens, and convicted felons being registered to vote in cities and entire swing-states across the country, which means your vote may be fully **canceled out in future elections**. **_American elections should be decided by American citizens._****[If you agree then please sign your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition to Amend the U.S. Constitution so the chaos we’re seeing now _never_ happens again in America.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z9k3vtc021qpd2rjcrrp3mptiq7m7p5a0plun8a0_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cpgmaoj1cth2bs)**Because, here’s the scary part:The last census took place in 2020. That was _before_ the 11.5 million illegal aliens who invaded our country under Joe Biden and Kamala Harris. To put it in context, there are only 8 states in America with a population over 11 million. So, it’s as if the radical Left just imported the 9th largest state in America. That’s more than North Carolina (10.8 million), Michigan (10 million), New Jersey (9.2 million), or Virginia (8.7 million).You get the picture. That’s why urgent action is needed to pass a Constitutional Amendment to ban illegal aliens from voting and from being counted for purposes of congressional and electoral vote apportionment. The next census in less than 6 years away. If those 11.5 million illegal aliens are counted in the census or are allowed to vote in the intervening years, you and I simply won’t have a country. **[It’s vitally important that your representatives in Washington and in your state legislature hear this demand directly from you.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zbrgk4bkvsfl8dmn8ha7o8jh3ebefnbs3pujj330_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cpgmaoj1cth2bs)** Because, quite honestly, they think they can pull a fast one on you. They think you and I will be so relieved to see the border secure again and criminal illegal aliens deported, that you and I will be oblivious to this threat lying dormant under our very eyes.No way.My name is Rebecca Weber. I’m the chairwoman of AMAC Action. **AMAC Action is the most influential advocacy group in the country when it comes to standing for the values of conservative Seniors.****We’ve got 72 chapters and 300 volunteer delegates, who are the “feet on the street” advocates who contact Members of Congress and state legislators in their district offices.** **Moreover, our chapters and delegates help organize Town Hall meetings with elected officials and candidates to enable those locally of our 2,000,000 AMAC members to meet, hear, and question them.****And you should also know that we now have more than 337,000 AMAC members who respond to our “calls-to-action” and weigh in with members of the** **U.S. House and Senate, as well as their state legislators on the issues.** Quite simply, when we speak, Washington listens. [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zlvpql5sc0jd08uq7rdqe4taf4l6ju6acn17j8l8_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cpgmaoj1cth2bs)**[And AMAC Action needs your help today in this do-or-die battle to pass a Constitutional Amendment to protect your vote from being canceled out by an illegal alien or a convicted felon.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zl9duifc3lf7ean1ijomollaj8qjiddub4l797e0_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cpgmaoj1cth2bs)** But I can’t do it without you. **No matter what issue you care about the most, if you and I don’t have a secure,_honest_ elections... none of it matters.**Inflation. Illegal immigration. Violent Crime. Drug use. Homelessness. The 2nd Amendment. Out of control spending. Social Security and Medicare insolvency. Right to Life. Indoctrination in our schools. Endless foreign wars. You name it. **[So please follow this link to sign your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition to Amend the U.S. Constitution](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z59n24glp374t7svotats7egus7n8beg5kfen2b8_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cpgmaoj1cth2bs)** so that AMAC Action can put your representatives in Washington and in the state legislature on notice with a simple demand: Namely, that you will not tolerate this erosion of your vote.Now, here’s the bad news:Most state constitutions grant voting rights to “every” citizen, open-ended language that liberal activists argue permits localities to authorize non-citizen and even illegal alien voting. States should amend their constitutions to instead permit “only” citizens to vote. But there’s good news, too:Seven states have _expressly_ banned non-citizen voting already: Alabama, Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Louisiana, North Dakota, and Ohio.**What’s more, voters approve of constitutional amendments to ban non-citizen voting by overwhelming margins. Nearly 77% of Ohio voters approved a measure in 2022, while nearly 63% of Colorado voters approved one in 2020.** This is a solution whose time has come. You and I can do this. **[That’s why, when you’ve signed your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition to Amend the U.S. Constitution](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zstj3hukf0cgmj34phqr0ccdpcgf2enm6urgmf98_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cpgmaoj1cth2bs), I'm also asking you to make a one-time contribution of $35 to give AMAC Action the resources to send out, collect, process, and tabulate millions of petitions.** The reality is, we don’t get a dime of taxpayer funding. Our funding comes from grassroots conservatives like you who care deeply about the future of America. This is important. _It means we can’t be bought._ On the other hand, the leftwing election fraud machine is funded by leftwing billionaires like Mark Zuckerberg and George Soros who are actively funneling _billions_ to dark money “non-profit” groups to “**reshape** ” our elections and our electorate.With that said, if you’re able to make a larger contribution – say $50, $75, $125, $250, $500, or even $1,000 – it would really be a life saver. Please hurry. In order to secure your vote in all future elections – and with 11.5 million illegals chomping to be included in the next census – **[your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition to Amend the U.S. Constitution is vitally important.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z84ae6e3fkppc25mkecn612gb310ckh662jjfmsg_rp22sh2s8i6eob4cpgmaoj1cth2bs)** Yes, this is about saving your vote from being canceled. It’s also about saving America.And it all starts with the straightforward premise that non-citizens and illegal aliens – no matter how many Kamala Harris and Joe Biden imported on their watch – should be banned from voting _and_ banned from being counted for apportioning congressional seats and electoral votes. Thank you in advance for joining the fight to secure your vote
